author: SeraphimOTE
title: Shut Down
content:
Great game back when it first released and the couple years afterwards, but they shot itself in the foot with a lot of these continuous removals of elements that made that game incredibly fun, as micro transactions and the amount of ads drastically increased (and the removal of the endless runner which was its main staple), I think it’s well worth it that the game should shut down, not saying this out of hate, but I don’t think anyone who enjoyed games when they first released (or at least, games that had a perfect structure and quality of life elements that not many complained about) would want to slowly see their favorite game die; it hollows itself out and all that remains is the image of what it once was

Goodbye to Minion Rush, I hope the devs learn from their mistakes, and perhaps, if they make a second game, to keep the qualities of when this game first released

title: The best game ever
content:
Minion Rush isn’t just the best game of all time to me, it’s a piece of my childhood. It was the kind of game you could open whenever you were bored and instantly feel happy. Running through all those different worlds as a Minion, collecting bananas, using power-ups, unlocking costumes, and trying to beat your highest score created memories that felt so simple but meant so much. It wasn’t about having the best graphics or being the biggest game in the world. It was about having fun. For so many people, Minion Rush was there during different parts of their childhood, and that’s what makes it special. It became more than just a mobile game; it became a little piece of our lives.

That’s why seeing Minion Rush leave the App Store hurts. A game that brought so many people happiness is becoming something we’ll have to remember instead of something we can always come back to. But even if the game eventually disappears, the memories it gave us won’t. We’ll remember the characters, the music, the ridiculous costumes, the races, the bananas, and all those hours spent trying to beat our best scores. Minion Rush may not be around forever, but what it meant to the people who played it will always remain. Sometimes the greatest games aren’t the ones with the biggest communities or the most awards, they’re the ones that make you smile years after you first played them. And for a lot of us, Minion Rush will always be that game.
